title: Agents see what a TUI looks like: emulator-rendered screens + screenshots judged by a vision model, in a self-improvement loop
description:
Operator, 2026-10-01, after hn6's WIP dashboard rendered as a staircase in a real terminal with wrong counts (r3x, gmo): 'is there a way an agent can see a tui and have a self evaluation/improvement loop?' z7w covers property tests (Bombadil terminal driver, Hegel for --json); this tick adds SEEING it.
1. Text view: run the TUI in a pty through a terminal emulator library (Go: charmbracelet/x/vt or vt10x) and expose the screen grid (cells + colours) as test helpers: assert no line starts mid-row (staircase), every frame fits WxH at 80x24 / 120x40 / 200x60, key-driven views (j/k, enter, e, esc) render. herdr `pane read` for live panes.
2. Image view: scripted sessions with Charm's `vhs` (tape files per view) producing PNGs; a vision-capable model judges each frame against the spec's target layout and a rubric (alignment, truncation, hierarchy: needs-you first, calm headline) and lists concrete defects. Locally any vision model; in the cloud a Workers AI vision model only (never claude in the cloud).
3. Loop + workflow: UI ticks carry a standard 'render evidence' requirement — emulator tests pass and the screenshots are attached to the worker report (linked from RESULT, stored as run artifacts); the worker iterates (fix → re-render → re-judge, bounded); the final-review job is given the screenshots and the vision verdict; the operator sees them from watch/status. Wire into the report linter (4m6) so a UI tick without render evidence is pushed back.
acceptance_criteria: [1] An emulator-backed render test helper exists and the ticfac watch dashboard has frame tests at three sizes that would have caught r3x. [2] `make render-evidence` (or equivalent) produces vhs screenshots for watch's views and a vision verdict JSON. [3] A UI tick's worker report without render evidence is pushed back by the linter; the review job receives the screenshots. [4] make gate passes.
